description: loop() and while() statements and their iteration cap. The two-argument while(cond, body) form is a dialect extension shared with projectM and Butterchurn; ns-eel2 registers while with one argument, so the same programs read while(exec2(body, cond)) there.

cases.name: loop(n, body) runs the body n times
a loop count truncates toward zero
a negative loop count runs the body zero times
a loop body may hold several statements separated by semicolons
while(cond, body) repeats until the condition is zero
a while() condition uses the close-factor threshold, like every other boolean context
cases.note: Pinned by the ns-eel2 source (WACUP/vis_milk2@de9625a): asm-nseel-x86-gcc.c:866-875, in nseel_asm_repeatwhile, takes fabs of the condition, fcomp's it against [g_closefact] (NSEEL_CLOSEFACTOR = 0.00001, ns-eel-int.h:56), and leaves the loop when the x87 C0 flag says |cond| is below it (testl $256 / jnz). Modern EEL2 boolifies the same way (nseel_asm_fptobool / EEL_BC_FPTOBOOL: fabs(v) >= NSEEL_CLOSEFACTOR). A condition of 1e-6 is therefore false before the first iteration: the body never runs, x stays 0 and n keeps its 1e-6. A condition of exactly 1e-5 still loops in the source; this case does not pin that boundary. The id names the question this case once asked (it was provisional, pinning exact zero) and is kept stable; the value was corrected on 2026-10-28.
